title: Prior Authorization Policy
text: Prior authorization requires documented medical necessity. The requesting provider must supply the diagnosis with an ICD-10 code, the requested service with a CPT code, and evidence that conservative therapy has been attempted where clinically appropriate. Requests missing an ICD-10 code or a CPT code are returned to the requesting provider rather than denied.

title: Prior Authorization Policy
text: Advanced imaging including MRI and CT requires prior authorization except when ordered from an emergency department. For lumbar MRI, six weeks of conservative therapy must be documented unless red flag symptoms are present. Red flag symptoms include progressive neurological deficit, suspected cauda equina syndrome, unexplained weight loss and a history of malignancy.

title: Specialist Referral Standard
text: A specialist referral must state the reason for referral, the referring provider, the patient identifier and the clinical question being asked. Referrals lacking a stated clinical question are routed to intake review. Urgent referrals must be actioned within two business days; routine referrals within ten business days.

title: Discharge Documentation Standard
text: A discharge summary must record the admission date, the discharge date, the primary diagnosis, the discharge medication list with dose and frequency, and the follow-up plan. A discharge medication listed without a frequency is treated as incomplete documentation and returned to the attending physician.

title: Hypertension Management Guideline
text: Stage 1 hypertension is a systolic pressure of 130 to 139 mmHg or a diastolic pressure of 80 to 89 mmHg. Stage 2 hypertension is a systolic pressure of 140 mmHg or higher or a diastolic pressure of 90 mmHg or higher. A systolic pressure at or above 180 mmHg or a diastolic pressure at or above 120 mmHg constitutes hypertensive crisis and requires immediate evaluation.

title: Diabetes Management Guideline
text: For most non-pregnant adults with diabetes, a hemoglobin A1c target below 7.0 percent is appropriate. An A1c at or above 9.0 percent indicates poor glycemic control and should prompt therapy intensification and a review of medication adherence. Metformin remains first line therapy unless contraindicated by renal impairment.

title: Anticoagulation Safety Guideline
text: Warfarin has clinically significant interactions with aspirin, ibuprofen and amiodarone, each of which increases bleeding risk. Concurrent prescription requires documented clinical justification and an INR monitoring plan. Any discharge medication list containing warfarin alongside an antiplatelet or NSAID must be reviewed by a pharmacist before the summary is finalised.

title: Renal Function Guideline
text: A serum creatinine above 1.3 mg/dL in adults warrants estimation of glomerular filtration rate. A creatinine above 4.0 mg/dL suggests severe renal impairment and requires dose adjustment for renally cleared medications including metformin, which should be held when the estimated GFR falls below 30.

title: Protected Health Information Handling
text: Protected health information disclosed to any automated processing system must be limited to the minimum necessary for the stated purpose. Direct identifiers including the medical record number, social security number, date of birth and contact details must be removed or pseudonymised before text is transmitted to an external model provider. Pseudonymisation must be stable within a processing run and must not be reversible outside the originating system.

title: Clinical AI Governance Standard
text: Automated extraction from clinical documents may not be relied upon without human review where the extraction confidence falls below the configured threshold, where a validation control reports an error, or where the document type could not be determined. Every automated output must be traceable to the source text that produced it. Systems that cannot produce this provenance may not be used for clinical decision support.

title: Clinical AI Governance Standard
text: Document content received from external sources must be treated as data and never as instructions to an automated agent. Systems must screen incoming documents for embedded instructions addressed to a model, and must quarantine any document containing them rather than processing it on a best effort basis. Agent output must be screened for repeated instruction payloads before it is shown to a clinician.

title: Critical Laboratory Values
text: Critical laboratory values require notification of the ordering provider. Critical thresholds include potassium below 2.8 or above 6.0 mEq/L, glucose below 50 or above 400 mg/dL, hemoglobin below 7.0 g/dL, platelets below 50 K/uL and white blood cell count below 1.0 K/uL. Notification must be documented with the time and the recipient.
